title: Rounded hypothesis recovers the real target
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, $k\ge 0$, and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. Suppose the function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ obtained through the coordinatewise binary-to-sign identification has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients. Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of coordinate subsets containing every subset $U$ whose real Fourier coefficient for $f$ has magnitude at least the threshold determined by the exact sparse-spectrum Goldreich–Levin input for $n,k$. Form the empirical Fourier hypothesis from the target's values on the corresponding deterministic samples and round its coefficients to granularity $2(1/2)^{k+1}$. The resulting real-valued Fourier sum equals the real-valued function associated to $f$ at every point of the sign cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
the binary-cube Fourier sparsity of the transported function is at most $2^{k+1}$
$\mathcal F$ is a finite family of coordinate subsets
every subset with Fourier coefficient magnitude at least the specified threshold belongs to $\mathcal F$
